tasks.title: repo skeleton, the one gate, and a bash test harness
acceptance: bin/ci.sh exists, is executable, and exits 0 on a tree with no tests
every tests/*.test.sh runs; any non-zero makes the whole gate non-zero and the failing suite is named
shellcheck is clean over bin/**.sh
the GitHub Actions workflow calls bin/ci.sh rather than restating its steps

tasks.title: fm-emit.sh, the only writer of the event log
acceptance: writes are serialised by a lock; 20 concurrent writers lose no lines and every line parses as JSON
an unknown type is rejected with a non-zero exit and nothing is written
an event carrying a summary must have both en and zh-TW, otherwise it is rejected
ci.sh fails if anything under bin/ or board/ appends to events.jsonl outside fm-emit.sh

tasks.title: fm-sync-prs.sh, which notices a merge on its own
acceptance: polls gh for pull request state and writes pr_opened, merged and closed back through fm-emit.sh
de-duplicates against the log by pull request number and state; running twice changes nothing
a merge the captain performs on GitHub is detected by the system itself, not reported to it by a person
exits non-zero without polluting the log when offline or when gh is not authenticated
tests drive it from recorded gh output and make no network call

tasks.title: fm-guard.sh and git hooks: nobody writes to main
acceptance: fm-guard.sh refuses main, master and a detached HEAD, and honours FM_PROTECTED
pre-commit blocks a commit on a protected branch and allows one on a feature branch
pre-push blocks a push whose target ref is a protected branch
the hooks are self-contained: they must not depend on bin/ existing in the worktree being committed to
branch protection on GitHub has enforce_admins on, since firstmate runs on the captain's own credentials

tasks.title: the adapter contract, the mock adapter, and the contract test
acceptance: mock.sh produces a scripted diff and reaches no network
the contract test pins the meaning of exit codes 0, 1 and 2
the contract test proves an adapter ran no git and no gh command
the contract test proves an adapter wrote nothing outside its worktree
claude.sh, cursor-agent.sh and gemini.sh all pass the same contract test

tasks.title: fm-gate.sh, the seven gates
acceptance: each of the seven gates has one passing and one blocking case, fourteen in all
gate 5 blocks a pull request whose new test stays green after the implementation is reverted
gate 5 passes a pull request whose new test goes red when the implementation is reverted
gate 4 blocks a diff that reaches outside the task's scope globs in tasks.json
gate 7 ignores an APPROVE string that did not come from the configured reviewer account
the exit code says which gate failed

tasks.title: fm-worker.sh: worktree, adapter, commit, pull request
acceptance: creates a worktree per task from main under state/worktrees/<task>
the prompt carries only the task spec, the relevant part of design.md, and skills/worker
commit and gh pr create are run by this script; the adapter never touches git
an adapter exiting 2 moves to the next vendor in config.yaml and emits vendor_unavailable
an adapter exiting 1 proceeds to the gates without falling back
the whole path runs on the mock adapter with no network

tasks.title: fm-review.sh: the reviewer sees only the diff
acceptance: the reviewer prompt contains the diff, the task spec and the acceptance criteria and nothing else
a test asserts the prompt contains no worker log, reasoning or worktree path
the reviewer's output is posted with gh pr comment by the script
only APPROVE:<task-id> is recognised by fm-gate.sh

tasks.title: fm-dispatch.sh: the DAG, the limit, and the green-light gate
acceptance: dispatches nothing and exits non-zero when the log holds no matching greenlit event
dispatches only tasks whose depends_on are all merged
never exceeds the concurrency in config.yaml
ci.sh fails when section 14 of design.md and tasks.json disagree

tasks.title: fm-decide.sh: a decision lands and firstmate wakes
acceptance: with bun present it uses fs.watch and returns within 200ms of the file appearing
without bun it falls back to a one-second poll with identical behaviour
it depends on neither fswatch, entr nor watchexec
a decision already on disk is not missed across a restart

tasks.title: board server: SSE, static files, hot reload
acceptance: binds 127.0.0.1 only
tails events.jsonl and pushes new events over SSE
a change under board/public/** pushes a reload event
no build step: bun run board/server.ts starts it
the SSE client reconnects on its own after a drop
the board reports only what the log already holds; it derives task stage from events rather than keeping its own view

tasks.title: board UI: the ship, the crew, the decision deck, the lanes, the log
acceptance: rewritten from the prototype in design/proposals, not copied from it
every crew pose is expressed as a .fig.s-<state> class so e2e asserts classes rather than diffing screenshots
status text belongs to its own figure and no two nameplates collide
drag a figure to turn it, drag the deck to turn the crew, double-click resets
prefers-reduced-motion is honoured
decks and hull are generated from one curve in one SVG, in the same projection as the crew; no mixing an elevation with perspective decks
every deck carries a bulwark and a riser wall, so a level reads as a level
brass is the only accent in the scene and the crew are the brightest layer
the ship has six rates from a one-mast cutter to a six-mast man-o'-war, up to 24 aboard; a crowd stacks onto more decks rather than stretching the hull
hull, decks, crew and bubbles all align to --deckY0 + row * --rowStep, and each deck plate is the same height so the crew plant to the same depth on every level
the whole sail hangs above the tallest crewman's head, asserted as sail.bottom <= highestHead.top
mast spacing follows the topmost deck's width and no mast sits outside it at any rate
the helm is a fixture of the topmost deck, placed by construction rather than by where firstmate happens to stand
the bow faces left, the end firstmate stands on, with the stern lantern to the right
barrel, port lid, muzzle flash and smoke all point the same way, toward the bow
gun ports and the figurehead render at fixed pixel sizes and do not deform with beam
the hull's gun ports, the flash positions and the sound schedule all come from one gun list; each flash sits exactly on its port and the number of reports equals the number of guns
twelve actions pooled by deck, with a separate pool for idle crew; with twelve or more aboard at least eight distinct actions are on screen at once
every action holds or stands at a prop; nothing mimes
each action declares its own arm animation and no state rule leaks one onto an action that did not
tools follow the job rather than the role, and state wins over action
crew alternate a weight shift and hop on independent offsets; shoes animate with their leg and the foot travels more than 6px per cycle
the hop animates translate rather than transform so it composes with the pose animations
each crewman carries a status bubble above his head with a tail pointing back at him, the border colour carrying state
deck spacing exceeds body height plus bubble height, so no bubble covers the crew on the deck above, verified from 3 to 24 aboard
the roster opens automatically once the bubbles drop the task title, and carries state, deck, task id and title, file scope, round, pull request and progress
the captain is drawn at the left of the decision deck, poses through idle, ready and order, and is draggable
the deck renders a merge card, the seven-gate checklist standing in for the diagram

a merge and an order each trigger an ahoy: the ship heels, guns or bell, the crew cheer, a banner. Sound is synthesised through Web Audio with no audio files, there is a mute control, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured
nothing in the celebration covers what is being celebrated
shared numbers have one source: CSS custom properties are written from the JavaScript constants, never declared twice

tasks.title: i18n: dictionaries, the tw2cn table, the hardcoded-string lint
acceptance: ui.en.json and ui.zh-TW.json hold exactly the same keys, and no value is empty
every key the page asks for exists in the dictionary
tw2cn.tsv covers the terms that differ between the two vocabularies, every row is two columns, and no term is listed twice
zh-CN is derived from zh-TW by the table at display time, so there is no third dictionary to fall out of step
the page holds no hardcoded Chinese: every string a reader sees comes from the dictionary
switching language makes no network and no model call

tasks.title: the /open endpoint and the read-only diff viewer
acceptance: any non-localhost origin gets a 403
a path resolving outside the repository gets a 403, with a test for the .. route and the symlink route
the editor command comes from config.yaml and defaults to code
a read-only viewer can show a file and a branch diff without leaving the board
a branch name carrying a shell metacharacter is refused, and an unknown branch is a 404 rather than a 500
every path-taking endpoint shares one check: resolve fully, then insist the real path sits inside the real root

tasks.title: the decision API, including merge cards
acceptance: after a POST, state/decisions/<id>.json exists and is valid JSON
e2e: choosing on the board releases fm-decide.sh within one second
posting the same decision twice is idempotent and creates no second file
kind=merge is supported: the card shows the seven gates, the diff stat, the files and the pull request link, answered with merge, send back or hold
choosing merge runs gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch from the script; a test asserts no path exists for firstmate to merge without the board
the board never merges directly: it writes the decision and calls bin/fm-merge.sh, which validates the pull request number and its state first

tasks.title: Playwright e2e and the GitHub Actions workflow
acceptance: every e2e uses the mock adapter and calls no model
chrome snapshots run in all three languages; interaction flows run in zh-TW only
GitHub Actions runs bin/ci.sh, the same file the local gate runs
a full CI pass completes in under 60 seconds locally
the gate itself is asserted to run the browser suite, not only CI asserted not to
every zh-CN assertion pins an expected string, derived the way the board derives it
a board under test binds a free port rather than a guessed one
a fixture is removed whether the test passed or not
the language mechanisms are covered one at a time
the sixty-second budget is measured, not hoped for

tasks.title: fm-protocol.sh: round three and its violations
acceptance: rounds one and two are not policed
round three with no ASK-PASS-CRITERIA from the worker is a violation, exit 3
a reviewer who never posts CRITERIA-COMPLETE leaves the list open, exit 4
after the list closes, a comment must cite an item on it, carry REGRESSION:, or be the APPROVE; anything else is a violation, exit 5
a comment from anyone but the configured reviewer does not trip it
it counts and reports how many items the closed list held
every violation is emitted so the captain sees the reviewer drip-feeding
the suite runs from recorded comment payloads and makes no network call

tasks.title: fm-diagram.sh: decision diagrams and the board embed
acceptance: each decision produces D-*.en.html and D-*.zh-TW.html
zh-CN is produced by post-processing the text nodes through tw2cn.tsv
only decisions the captain must rule on produce a diagram; routine events do not
the board embeds them in an iframe and swaps src with the language
the suite that covers it lives where bin/ci.sh runs it
generated diagrams do not trip the hardcoded-string lint, which scans authored pages
requesting a decision draws its diagram, so the board never HEADs a file nobody wrote
a drawing authored for one language and not another is refused rather than served unevenly

tasks.title: fm-reconcile.sh: reconciling after a crash
acceptance: replaying events.jsonl rebuilds the whole state with no snapshot
walks state/worktrees and gh pr list to find orphans
a worker whose pid is gone is marked worker_crashed and redispatched
reconciling is idempotent: two runs leave the same state
a merged pull request whose event carried no task is repaired from the branch name
it prints what it would change and changes nothing with --dry-run

tasks.title: self-update and sync-skills
acceptance: a skill-update task travels the same pull request and the same seven gates as any other
no path exists that edits skills/ without a pull request, and a test asserts it
sync-skills imports into skills/vendor/ one way and never writes back
a lint fails on vendor-specific syntax inside skills/

tasks.title: fm-cleanup.sh: a worker removes its own worktree and nothing else
acceptance: removes state/worktrees/<task> and the branch's registration, after that task's pull request is merged
refuses any path that does not resolve to a direct child of the repository's own worktree root
refuses a path escaping through .. or through a symlink, with a test for each
refuses the repository root, the main worktree, and a path belonging to another repository
refuses while the pull request is still open, so an unmerged branch is never swept away
is idempotent: cleaning an already-clean task changes nothing and exits 0
every worktree lives under one root inside the repository, so the system stays self-contained

tasks.title: fm-run.sh: one turn of the whole loop, and an end-to-end proof of it
acceptance: fm-run.sh once dispatches what is ready and advances every task in flight by one step
it dispatches nothing before a greenlit event
all seven gates green asks the captain rather than merging
nothing merges until a decision file exists
an end-to-end suite runs dispatch to merged pull request with the mock adapter, a bare remote on disk and a gh stub - no network, no model
the suite asserts the log records greenlit, dispatched, commit_pushed, pr_opened, review_opened, decision_requested and merged
the worktree is gone after the merge

tasks.title: the adapter verdict: a vendor that fails silently is not one that worked
acceptance: an adapter reports unavailable when its CLI prints an outage and exits 0
a finished run whose own output discusses logins, rate limits or 429 is done, not an outage
a verdict reads only the bytes its own run added to the shared fallback log
each adapter is asserted to produce the invocation its CLI documents, not merely to be handed the prompt
the reviewer falls back through the same chain as the worker, from one implementation
no vendor runs twice however the fallback list is written
a review round must carry APPROVE or REJECT; anything else is an engine that failed, exits 3 and emits review_failed
a failed round keeps the engine's log under state/reviews and says where it is
fm-run reports a reviewer that was unavailable or produced no verdict instead of swallowing it
review_failed and worker_crashed read as blocked on the board, in counts as well as lanes
every stage the board maps is a type fm-emit will write
no stage of bin/ci.sh reads standard input, and a suite is handed /dev/null
the hygiene lint is asserted to be linting the suites it was given
no script dispatches a child without closing standard input, proved by a probe that blocks forever if it is open
the gate lints bin/adapters as well as bin, which bin/*.sh does not reach
work in the worktree is never discarded because the verdict read an outage
wording never decides finally: the caller supplies the evidence and work beats a signature
a vendor named in config.yaml with no adapter behind it is a configuration error, not an outage
a fixture that swaps a script out is paired with its restore by the harness, and a hand-rolled one fails the gate
the gate names every script that dispatches without closing standard input
an exit code never overrules produced work, in the adapters or in either caller
every signature is shaped like a failure and is read against a healthy transcript as well as a failing one
a configuration error is found before any vendor runs
each attempt reads only its own output: its own directory and its own slice of the shared log
a file that is meant to be sourced never carries the standard-input redirect

tasks.title: the option loop: eleven scripts spin for ever on a flag with no value
acceptance: no script loops for ever when a flag arrives with nothing after it
every one of them exits 64 and says which flag
the gate refuses a shift 2 that has not checked it has two
the probe runs under an alarm, because a test for a hang would hang the gate rather than fail it

tasks.title: the crew are agents, not pull requests
acceptance: a crewman is an agent that is working, not a task and not a pull request
the crew comes from the actors in the event log, derived by the server
an agent's bubble says which task it is on, and the roster says the same
two agents on two tasks are two crewmen; one agent that has moved between tasks is one
github is not an agent and is never aboard
the ship's rate follows the number of agents, which is the concurrency, not the backlog
the captain is not crew: he is drawn beside the cards, from the same pending deck the cards come from, and nothing else derives him
an agent that has finished its run is not aboard, whatever became of the task
a run says when it ends, on every exit path including the ones that give up
no script names a signal alongside EXIT in one trap: the handler runs and execution continues, and kill stops working
a suite that prints command-not-found cannot report green: the gate reads what the run said

tasks.title: one exit code for a usage error, in every script
acceptance: every usage error in every script exits 64, and every refusal to write exits 1
the gate enforces it rather than the design merely stating it
each converted path has an assertion that fails if it goes back

tasks.title: the lints are blind to the files that carry them
acceptance: the pipe-into-grep lint reads tests/ as well as bin/, which is where most of the pipelines are

a file is no longer exempted whole by # fm:lint-source: a LINE says it quotes a shape rather than runs it, and every other line in that file is judged - today the marker takes bin/ci.sh and bin/fm-config.sh out of the shift-2 stage and the pipe-into-grep stage entirely, and those are the two files that hold both rules
every site the widened lints report is converted or marked, and the count is pinned so a new one cannot arrive unnoticed
the marker is tested from both sides: a marked line does not fire the stage and an unmarked one does

tasks.title: a second round the worker cannot see, and a question nobody hears
acceptance: a worker dispatched on a task whose branch already has an open pull request finds that pull request itself, without being told the number
on a later round the prompt carries what review has said and the failing check, whether or not --pr was passed

the lookup keeps GitHub's exit status: answered-and-none carries on and opens a pull request, could-not-answer stops the run before the engine rather than building a blind prompt and pushing at a pull request nobody looked for
the worker's .fm-say.md reaches the pull request on any round where one exists, and the run says which pull request it went to

a message that could not be posted is an error the run reports, not a line on standard error nobody reads: asking is the whole of that round and a question that went nowhere leaves the task deadlocked

the worker's own lookup is the only path there can be: fm-dispatch never restarts a task whose pull request is open, so it has no number to pass, and the suite says so rather than the design claiming it

tasks.title: the red check reaches the worker as an empty block
acceptance: modern /actions/runs/<run>/job/<job> links fetch the workflow run; legacy /runs/<job> links fetch via gh run view --job, including query strings and fragments, without confusing job IDs with workflow run IDs

the stub answers the way gh answers - real link shapes and strict run view arguments that distinguish job IDs from workflow run IDs and refuse an id or namespace it does not recognise - so malformed selections fail the prompt-content tests
the block the worker is handed is asserted by its CONTENT reaching the prompt, not by gh having been called

a check whose log cannot be fetched says so in the prompt rather than leaving an empty block, because an empty block is indistinguishable from a green run and the worker spends its round asking about it

tasks.title: firstmate startup contract
acceptance: A concise canonical startup contract and thin Claude/Codex entrypoints route a top-level interactive session to firstmate immediately, while an explicitly dispatched worker or reviewer retains its assigned role; entrypoints link to the canonical contract rather than duplicating instructions.

The default firstmate plans, dispatches, monitors, coordinates remediation and submits decisions through the repository scripts; it does not implement production code or run git/gh mutations itself. Document the actual scripts and their limitations, including gate failures that require explicit remediation coordination.

Existing user authorization persists across turns and routine authorized work proceeds without repeated confirmation. Scope decisions and captain merge approval still go through the board, and firstmate does not infer captain merge approval from a request to finish all PRs.

Startup inspects resumable task state, open PRs, worktrees and live herdr panes before launching work; it resumes existing agents instead of duplicating them, checks herdr availability within the managed session, and launches actual future worker/reviewer processes in visible panes. A conversation subagent alone is not evidence that a herdr worker exists.

Startup starts or reuses the captain board and opens it using the available browser mechanism, verifies observable results, and never claims a board, worker, test, hook removal, commit or PR action succeeded without evidence.

All relevant role skills are English portable Markdown with provider-independent valid metadata. No vendor-specific syntax occurs inside skills/. Claude/Codex-specific loading conventions may appear only in their thin root entrypoints. Resolve existing role skills and links coherently rather than creating competing startup sources.

Firstmate, worker and reviewer instructions coherently capture the round-three closed-list review protocol, subsequent original-list/regression-only enforcement, and final-only reviewer verdict provenance; intermediate text or quoted APPROVE/REJECT cannot be treated as the final review decision.

Role instructions distinguish tests actually executed and their observable results from unverified claims, require honest limitations, and distinguish static English instruction prose from dynamic user-facing summaries that require both en and zh-TW.

There is no required reliance on lavish or no-mistakes in startup or role workflows. Verification uses the repository checks and actual GitHub CI evidence, with captain decisions retaining their established board workflow.

Changes remain documentation/instructions and narrowly useful skill metadata or link-structure validation. Do not add arbitrary prose-grep assertions or model/API-dependent CI. Update README and design references so future Claude and Codex sessions discover the same role contract without conversational history.

tasks.title: localized two-stage captain decisions, literal custom orders and confirmed outcome effects
acceptance: Every new decision has one concise task-specific explanation, a bespoke before/after change diagram and concrete advantages and costs for its A/B/C options. Remove repeated nested card framing, titles, lane strips, buttons and checklists from embedded diagrams. A generic workflow diagram is not a substitute for the actual proposed change.

Add validated structured localized decision input to fm-decide and document its shared server/diagram/frontend contract. Author dynamic titles, explanations, before/after labels, option descriptions, advantages/costs and outcome feedback in en and zh-TW. Derive zh-CN through the existing conversion semantics, extending its table where necessary for complete actual displayed content. Locale changes update entire content, not only controls; event summaries retain en and zh-TW.

Reject malformed new localized payloads before partial writes or replacing existing decisions. Keep legacy title-only records readable with explicit missing-detail feedback; never fabricate translations, task-specific diagrams or tradeoffs from missing author input. Firstmate supplies missing content before presenting a new decision as complete.

Use lightweight repository-native HTML/inline SVG and the existing authored-fragment mechanism where useful; no image generation, Figma, lavish or external model/rendering dependency. Escape untrusted dynamic text and validate data boundaries; distinguish trusted authored fragments from data, and verify markup-like text cannot inject scripts or controls.

Add behavioral coverage for two materially different decisions with distinct before/after diagrams and option tradeoffs, no nested duplicate content, complete en/zh-TW/zh-CN locale switching, malformed/missing localization, legacy records, safe text rendering, authored-fragment selection and derived zh-CN, as well as all effect scenarios below.

Restore the original two-stage decision interaction demonstrated by design/proposals/2026-09-20-captain-board/prototype.html (pick handler near line 928 and separate submit control near line 1519) and design/design.md Captain/Ahoy sections. Selecting A/B/C updates only local selection and the captain's half-drawn sword pose: no decision file, POST or other network mutation. A distinct explicit confirmation submits the selected option and raises the sword; no selection means confirmation is unavailable. Preserve A/B/C meanings, merge authorization and truthful request outcome handling. Keep the captain visible until the final acknowledgement/effect completes even when its last card disappears.

On explicit confirmation, show the order being sent; on successful recorded acknowledgement, animate the whole visible crew in staggered response with the captain's raised sword, two helm spins, and AYE, CAPTAIN! / ORDERS AWAY. The later audio override keeps order speech, bell and whistle off. English cries remain invariant across locales; surrounding interface content localizes. Honor persistent mute and reduced-motion with accessible static acknowledgement. A pending/failed request has distinct truthful feedback, and a recorded order is never presented as a successful merge: merge broadside/banner and cannon require actual confirmed merge success.

Confirmed merge effects follow newly observed merge-event identity, not changes in the task-derived merged count. A merge for a task absent from the currently loaded design/tasks.json still produces one celebration. Duplicate SSE snapshots, explicit refreshes, repeated delivery and reconnects do not replay an already handled event; initial historical state does not replay old celebrations. Multiple newly observed outcomes are not silently collapsed into a single count delta.

The decision path provides an observable stable identity and outcome for recorded decisions without depending on a separate fm-decide --await process. Preserve bin/fm-emit.sh as the only append path for events and avoid duplicate semantic events if an existing waiter also observes the response. If satisfying this requires changing scripts outside this scope, stop for a scope decision rather than editing them.

Routine state refreshes do not replace or reset active captain/ship effect state before its visible completion. Crew and task data can continue updating during the effect. Do not invent agents, task progress, successful merges or lifecycle events for visual feedback.

A merge helper failure or request/network error shows persistent accessible failure feedback and no successful-merge broadside/banner. An HTTP response that records a decision while reporting merge failure is not treated as merge success. Duplicate recorded requests do not invent a new successful outcome.

Respect prefers-reduced-motion with a readable static outcome acknowledgement instead of suppressing all feedback. Audio mute persists, audio is optional, and browser autoplay refusal never prevents the decision or its visible feedback. Localize new interface text through English and zh-TW dictionaries and the existing zh-CN derivation; event summaries retain both en and zh-TW.

Add fail-first behavioral browser coverage for actual decision submission and resulting captain/order effects, a real merge event for a task absent from task definitions, duplicate/reconnected state delivery, state refresh during an effect, failed merge, and reduced-motion feedback. Assertions must observe outcomes and effect lifetime, not merely grep source or click the manual Ahoy demonstration button. Test fixtures use isolated local state and stub merge execution, never real captain decisions or model/network APIs. Also assert selection alone performs no POST/file write, explicit confirmation submits the selected option exactly once, captain sword poses follow selection/send/outcome, captain persists after the final card disappears, the whole crew acknowledges in staggered order, and cries remain English across locales.

Run the repository CI and relevant browser tests, record actual observed results and limitations, and establish that new regressions fail with the implementation removed. Update the relevant design contract and task metadata to describe the shipped behavior without claiming that instruction prose or a manually triggered effect proves the complete decision path.

Add a genuine fourth custom/free-text captain choice, distinct from predefined A/B/C and distinct from a note attached to A. Selecting it and typing remain local with no mutation until explicit confirmation; initially no option is selected and no action is sent. Persist a stable distinct chosen value such as custom plus its authored text as bounded validated data, never shell evaluation or implicit merge approval. Reject empty/whitespace-only or over-limit custom input before persistence; escape markup and preserve its exact valid text through server storage, state/watch roundtrip and firstmate consumption. Localize choice label, hint, validation and outcome feedback in all supported locales; do not translate or reinterpret the captain's authored text. A custom order always remains a captain decision for interpretation, never an automatic arbitrary command or a merge-equivalent A. Browser and server tests cover selection/confirmation, Unicode, escaping, limits, stored roundtrip and proof that custom text cannot trigger merge.

Apply the later captain audio override: disable Ahoy-related speech, bell and whistle cues without substitute sounds or global mute. Preserve visible order/merge effects and invariant English cries. An actually confirmed merge retains synthesized cannon reports; persistent mute silences them, initial history stays silent, and stable event identities prevent replay across duplicate SSE snapshots, refresh and reconnect. Selection, orders, rejected submissions and unconfirmed/failed merges produce no audio. Browser autoplay refusal never breaks decisions, reduced motion remains independent, no external audio requests occur, and the board never touches an unrelated browser speech queue. Tests use fake Web Audio/speech APIs to prove cannon eligibility, unwanted-cue absence, mute and deduplication.

Pending decisions precede the ship and active work; captain, gate, review, working and queued lanes exclude completed tasks. A native initially collapsed history preserves every merged/closed identity and PR, truthful separate counts and session disclosure state through refresh and locale changes.

Use at least 16px primary and 13px secondary text, 20px decision titles and 44px choice/confirm targets. Three locales reflow at 320/390/768/1280 widths and 200 percent text without page overflow or clipping decision meaning.

The helm follows the original left firstmate/deck anchor; bow remains left and stern right. Exactly one human captain remains on the real ship deck through zero pending cards, selection, confirmation, acknowledgement, errors, refresh and reduced motion, without changing agent concurrency.

Replay full event history for stable actor identity, authored en/zh-TW activity and truthful phase. Derive CN, retain dispatch descriptions through technical events, avoid cross-run contamination and scalar-title translation guesses, label missing descriptions and unknown phases, and display only explicitly bounded progress.

Directed order/work/approve/reject handoffs resolve real participants from task and lifecycle events, retain stable event identities and visible travel/reaction across refresh/locale/resize, and never replay initial or duplicate history. Missing or ambiguous participants produce honest localized static feedback. Restore individual/deck drag, pointer cancellation and double-click reset without interfering with captain controls.

Focused isolated browser checks cover history geometry and persistence, all locales and widths, always-aboard deck bounds and left helm at ship-size boundaries, retained activity beyond 40 events, directed travel endpoints and pointer capture, reduced motion and the original real decision/custom/outcome/audio cases. Firstmate coordinates full CI and publication.

tasks.title: managed firstmate session defaults
acceptance: Ship a documented session bootstrap with vendor-neutral role context injection for the declared supported adapters. Native Claude/Codex root entrypoints remain thin routes to the shared contract. Top-level sessions default immediately to firstmate; explicitly dispatched workers/reviewers retain their roles and never launch a crew. Do not claim arbitrary engines automatically load AGENTS.md, or claim unsupported engines are ready.

Managed Herdr transport is shipped in the repository and enabled by default when HERDR_ENV=1. Detect and use the supported installed Herdr interface truthfully; launch real worker/reviewer processes in visible panes named by task and role through the normal adapter path. A clean clone needs no ignored runtime transport wrappers or global startup hooks. Missing/unsupported Herdr transport is surfaced clearly and never reported as successful visible dispatch.

Every dispatched worker and reviewer receives a distinct human-readable crew name, such as worker-mira-t035-r2 or reviewer-noah-t018-r8, with role/task/run identity and a collision suffix when needed. These are machine crew labels, not claims of actual human accounts. Keep the canonical name within Herdr's 32-character limit and supported syntax, retaining role prefixes for existing consumers unless explicit role fields are verified throughout. Use the identical canonical name in process invocation/context, Herdr pane/sidebar identity, board event actor, logs and final result metadata. Names remain stable during a run; different active workers/reviewers never share a name, and retries receive a distinct run identity. Reject or disambiguate colliding requested aliases without hiding the mapping. Do not inconsistently rename already-live actors; apply new naming coherently to new runs and document the examples in role skills.

Propagate canonical identity through the actual shipped fm-run, fm-dispatch, fm-worker, fm-review and adapter entrypoints. Default managed execution and ownership-safe lifecycle must work when those real entrypoints are invoked, not only through an unused standalone helper. Explicitly document whether vendor fallback retains the logical run actor or creates an attempt identity; preserve one unambiguous canonical mapping across panes, events and artifacts.

The completed/agent_finished event retires exactly the canonical actor for that run and cannot remove a concurrent worker or reviewer. Test concurrent same-task runs, worker-versus-reviewer runs, retries, requested-name collisions, naming-limit normalization, vendor fallback and exact actor removal through the real orchestration entrypoints with isolated mocks.

Pane lifecycle ownership is explicit and verifiable. Before attempting automatic close, durably persist final result, logs, process exit status and a structured final completion status (or equivalent explicit final-answer-only task-status contract). Process exit zero alone does not establish completed work: blocked, failed, incomplete, missing or ambiguous status retains the pane and artifacts. Immediately before closing, verify the exact recorded owned pane/run/task/terminal/shell identity and observed shell-only terminal state; never attempt to close an observed caller, unowned, reused, mismatched or busy pane. Refuse and retain on uncertainty. Use the installed Herdr CLI's available checks; do not require an unsupported atomic conditional-close API or upstream Herdr implementation. Document the unavoidable check-to-close race with an unrelated external client honestly instead of promising mathematical atomicity. Concurrent runs retain distinct ownership/artifacts; default close applies only to positively verified completed owned runs.

Outside managed Herdr, retain normal supported adapter execution and vendor fallback. Availability reflects real executable/transport checks and actual results; do not turn a transport failure, empty response or partial output into fabricated success. Existing adapter result/verdict provenance and failure behavior remain compatible.

Session bootstrap inspects actual live tasks/processes/panes and existing state before launch, resumes supported existing work without duplicate workers, and starts or reuses only the correct-root captain board after observable server checks. Open the board through an available supported mechanism and report opener/page-verification limitations honestly. Honor configured concurrency and preserve interrupted work.

Expose an actual cancellable decision-watch process using the existing repository watcher path. Its live/stopped/failed status and identity must be observable, with durable observed decision results. Reuse an existing matching watch rather than duplicating it. Do not claim that a background process wakes a completed conversational agent turn or that no live process is continuously monitoring.

Session defaults are enabled without requiring per-task transport toggles or opt-in prompts. Provide a documented explicit user opt-out for managed transport, successful-owned-pane auto-close and decision watching where applicable. Preserve prior user authorization for routine work; scope/product choices and merge approval still go through the captain board. User authorization of this self-update is not a fabricated board choice or merge approval.

Use stable per-run execution artifacts so edits to live source scripts or wrappers cannot shift a running shell's execution or duplicate adapter work. Snapshot the supported execution path as needed and retain enough run identity/evidence to distinguish source changes from the code actually executed. Do not edit or replace artifacts that an active run is reading.

Update shared role skills with the actual shipped startup/lifecycle behavior and durable session lessons: honest evidence, actual tests versus claims, final-only current-head reviewer provenance, original closed-list protocol, continued authorization and resumable state. Include firstmate's requirement for bespoke decision change diagrams, option tradeoffs and authored en/zh-TW dynamic content with derived zh-CN, while explicitly distinguishing requirements from board implementation still pending under T-034.

No dependency on lavish, no-mistakes, global hooks, environment-specific ignored scripts or undeclared external tooling is introduced. Keep skills portable English Markdown with valid provider-neutral metadata; use root entrypoints or the launcher for vendor-specific loading. Document exact support and failure boundaries, including effects/locale fixes not yet shipped.

Add meaningful fail-first clean-clone/mock tests for role injection, default managed and non-managed paths, ownership-safe pane close, caller/reused/busy protection, result persistence before close, transport/output failure, concurrent identities, explicit opt-out, board reuse, live cancellable watch and per-run source stability. CI uses no real model API, real user panes, external accounts or actual captain decisions. Run repository CI and relevant tests and report observed results and remaining limitations.

Implementation remains inside this exact scope. If watcher implementation, board production files or additional exact files must change, identify the required files and reason to firstmate before implementation; do not silently broaden scope or claim guarantees that the shipped entrypoints cannot enforce.

Treat a platform limitation as a bounded limitation: implement all independently satisfiable accepted criteria and report remaining evidence/gaps precisely. An unavailable atomic conditional-close operation is not a prerequisite to the authorized checked-close policy. Tests must distinguish rc=0 plus blocked/failed/incomplete final status from completed status and retain the former, while proving observed caller/reused/busy/mismatched identities are never targeted for close using mocks, not real user panes.

In a managed Herdr session, every newly dispatched worker and reviewer owns a dedicated new tab with one owned root pane; never split the captain's tab or another user's view. Create the tab with the supported --no-focus option, retain caller tab/pane identity, and verify the caller's focus remains unchanged. Use the same unique human-readable role/task/run canonical crew label for the tab, its agent pane/sidebar, board actor, process context and run artifacts, within Herdr naming limits. Review and retry/continuation launches follow this default too; explicit resumed live runs retain their verified identity without duplicate agents.

Record ownership of the created tab and its single root pane together with the existing run/task/terminal/shell identities. Completion auto-close remains guarded: first persist a positively completed task status and final artifacts, then immediately verify unchanged ownership, exact identities, shell-only terminal state and that the tab still contains only that owned pane. Retain the tab/pane on uncertainty, failure, blocked/incomplete result, reuse, a user-added pane, shared-tab membership or observed busy state. Never close the caller, an unowned tab, or a shared tab, and never use unconditional whole-tab close.

Closing a positively verified owned pane may cause its unchanged single-pane tab to disappear under Herdr's normal behavior; this is not authority to close arbitrary tabs. Document the available CLI's check-to-close race honestly. Tests use fake Herdr interfaces to assert default tab creation with --no-focus, one root pane per worker/reviewer, caller focus preservation, exact crew identity mapping and refusal after tab membership or ownership changes. Do not exercise closure on real user panes in CI.

The isolated crew-end-to-end fixture copies the shipped fm-herdr.py dependency and exercises real worker-to-board identity and exact completion removal without outer-checkout helpers. D-335 authorizes this additional fixture path.

Before updating firstmate decision instructions, inspect the final T-034 fm-decide.sh and fm-run.sh version identified by firstmate and its acceptance/tests read-only. Replace title-only examples with its actual --details authored en/zh-TW contract, exact validation and refusal handling; preserve user-authored custom choices and dynamic locale requirements. Clearly mark the integration dependency until that version lands.

tasks.title: truthful crew progress
acceptance: Document in design.md a mid-run reporting contract with three layers: (1) mechanical lifecycle phases emitted only from script-known nodes, (2) authored data.activity {en, zh-TW} that never invents task-specific progress from scalar titles, (3) optional bounded progress only when a true denominator exists (for example done/total). State explicitly that the 2026-09-20 captain-board prototype's random pct tick is demo-only and must not be promoted as product truth.

Remove or disable any client-side invention of percentages from coarse lifecycle state (including the working/gate/review/captain → fixed pct map). Bubbles and roster show a progress bar only when the crew payload carries explicitly bounded progress; otherwise no bar and no fake percent.

Board /api/state (or equivalent) crew payloads expose authored activity, optional bounded progress, crew_name and a truthful phase derived from event replay per T-034 rules: retain activity beyond the recent-event window, label missing activity explicitly, and never fabricate mid-run copy for visuals.

Producers: fm-worker.sh, fm-review.sh and managed herdr transport emit phase/activity (and bounded progress when applicable) through fm-emit.sh at script-known nodes such as adapter started, tests running, commit pushed, review opened, verdict signed. Cursor/Claude/Codex/Gemini share the same path; do not add vendor-only progress invention. Heartbeat-only pane text is not board state until emitted.
Throttle or coalesce high-frequency updates so the event log stays usable; a still-running heartbeat may refresh activity on an interval without claiming percent complete.

Add fail-first tests for: no bar without bounded progress, activity round-trip en/zh-TW on crew payload, phase retention across technical events, and refusal to treat missing progress as a percentage. Run repository CI and report observed results.
Implementation stays on this task's branch and PR only. Do not land this work on the T-035 / PR #51 branch. Scope remains the listed globs; widen only via captain decision.

tasks.title: fm-worker.sh must reuse an existing task branch, not re-derive its name
acceptance: This task's own entry, exactly as given here, must be committed into design/tasks.json on this task's branch (matching the existing convention used by other tasks that define themselves within their own diff), so the reviewer and fm-gate.sh can find it.

fm-worker.sh already computes branch_guess from existing refs/heads before deriving a fresh branch name from the task's current title. When branch_guess is non-empty, the worker must use it as the branch to continue, never independently recompute a name from the (mutable) title and fall through to creating a new branch from base when that recomputed name happens not to match any existing local or remote ref. Recomputing a slug from title is reserved for the case where branch_guess is genuinely empty (no existing ref for this task).

Add a fail-first regression test: given an existing local (or remote-only) branch for a task whose current title would slug/truncate to a different name (reproducing the observed case where an untruncated historical branch name no longer matches the current cut -c1-28 slug), running fm-worker.sh --task <id> must reuse that existing branch and worktree, and must never create a second branch from base for a task that already has one. Assert this without exercising a live captain decision, model or network API.
Do not change the branch-continuity behavior for a task that genuinely has no existing branch (branch_guess empty): it must still create a fresh branch from base exactly as today.
Run bin/ci.sh and report the observed exit status/duration for this branch.

tasks.title: fm-gate.sh's gate 3 must run the full local gate at the budget design.md already authorizes
acceptance: This task's own entry, exactly as given here, must be committed into design/tasks.json and this row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch, matching the convention other self-registering tasks use.

design/design.md section 10 already documents that bin/ci.sh defaults to a 180-second budget, that GitHub sets FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS=600, and that 'Firstmate runs the same full local gate with FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS=600 bash bin/ci.sh before publication.' Do not redesign this; gate3() in bin/fm-gate.sh currently invokes the detached worktree's bin/ci.sh with no FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS set at all, so it silently runs at the bare 180-second default instead of the 600-second budget the design already authorizes for this exact use. Fix gate3() to invoke bin/ci.sh with FM_CI_MAX_SECONDS=600 in its environment, matching GitHub's own budget and design.md's stated firstmate practice.

This changes only the elapsed-time budget gate3 runs under; it must not change or weaken any functional check inside bin/ci.sh, and a genuinely failing suite (shellcheck, a red bash/bun/playwright test, the dag check, etc.) must still fail gate3 exactly as before, regardless of budget.

Add a fail-first regression test in tests/gate.test.sh: a fixture whose full suite takes longer than 180 seconds but less than 600 (a controllable/fake duration, not a real sleep long enough to be flaky) must pass gate3 under the fixed code and must fail it under the old bare-default behavior. Do not depend on real wall-clock timing beyond what is needed to distinguish the two budgets deterministically.
Run bin/ci.sh and report the observed exit status/duration for this branch.

tasks.title: firstmate never loses a captain order it did not act on
acceptance: Incident this task answers (2026-09-23): the captain answered D-047 on the board. The session watcher started by fm-session.sh recorded it within a second in state/session/observed/D-047.json, but nothing woke the conversational firstmate: its turn had ended and a watcher only writes to disk. Firstmate did not act until the captain asked. This task's own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

Managed flow: `bin/fm-session.sh status` reports every observed decision that firstmate has not yet acknowledged (id, task, kind, chosen, custom text, decision timestamp), in the machine-readable output and as a short human summary. Add an explicit acknowledgement, for example `bin/fm-session.sh ack --decision D-nnn`, which records a durable acknowledgement under state/session/ without deleting the observation, the decision file or any event. Acknowledgement is idempotent; acknowledging an id with no observation is refused with a clear message. `status` and `start` stay read-only toward decisions; they never consume, merge or answer one.

Skill (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, portable English, no vendor-specific syntax): state the rule that a session watcher or an observation file never wakes a conversational agent. After every decision request, firstmate starts a notifying wait whose completion reaches the conversation (`bin/fm-decide.sh --await <id> --repo <root>` run as a background task the host reports on when it finishes). Firstmate does not end a turn while any card is pending without such a live wait. At the start of every turn and before ending one, firstmate runs `bin/fm-session.sh status`, acts on every unacknowledged observed decision, then acknowledges it. Keep the existing statements that exit zero is observation, not approval.

Fail-first tests in tests/session.test.sh: an observed-but-unacknowledged decision appears in status; after ack it no longer appears; ack is idempotent and refuses an unknown id; status never removes or rewrites decision, pending or observation files. tests/skills.test.sh keeps passing with the updated skill. Run bin/ci.sh and report observed results.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.

tasks.title: a worker that changed files still opens its PR when it also leaves a note
acceptance: Incident (2026-09-23, T-041 round 1): the claude adapter runs with --permission-mode acceptEdits, so the worker edited every file but could not execute tests. It wrote a completion note in .fm-say.md saying so. fm-worker.sh (the asked/spoke block near 'asking is premature') treats any .fm-say.md as a question, so on a first round with no PR it keeps the note in state/unsent/ and exits 73. It opens no PR, even though the worktree had real changes. This task's own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

When a round changed files in the worktree and also left a .fm-say.md, fm-worker.sh commits and pushes as usual, opens the pull request if none exists, then posts the note as a PR comment. Only a round that left a note and changed nothing, on a branch with no PR, keeps the existing 'asking is premature' behaviour (note kept under state/unsent/, worker_crashed event, non-zero exit). .fm-say.md is still never committed.

skills/worker/SKILL.md: a worker whose adapter cannot execute commands does not stop or ask because it cannot run tests. It finishes the work, says in its note which checks it could not run, and ends with WORKER_COMPLETE:<task>. Verification is the gates' job and the pull request's required GitHub check. Keep the existing closed-list and ASK-PASS-CRITERIA rules unchanged.

Fail-first tests in tests/worker.test.sh with the mock adapter and the existing gh stub: a round-one adapter that changes a file and writes .fm-say.md ends with an opened PR and the note posted as a comment; a round-one adapter that only writes .fm-say.md still opens no PR and keeps the note under state/unsent/. Evidence is the pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates; this task does not require the worker to execute tests itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.

tasks.title: a completed run's pane actually closes
acceptance: Incident (2026-09-23/24): every run that finished with status completed was retained with 'retained: pane identity or state changed'. That covered four of four today: reviewer-noah-t040-r58, reviewer-noah-t041-r56, reviewer-noah-t042-r57 and worker-mira-t042-r55. Firstmate closed each pane by hand after checking. Observed on real Herdr: after the adapter exits and the pane is back at an idle shell prompt, with the recorded shell_pid alive and no children, `herdr pane list` still reports agent_status 'working'. Pane id, terminal id, tab, workspace, label and the fm_actor/fm_task/fm_run tokens all still matched the ownership record. close_owned() in bin/fm-herdr.py refuses unless agent_status is 'idle' or 'done', so on real Herdr it can never close. This task's own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

close_owned() stops gating on agent_status. Idleness is decided by the existing process-info shell_only check. Every other retain condition stays exactly as it is: incomplete or blocked result, missing evidence, ownership change, pane/terminal/tab/workspace/label/token mismatch, busy or changed shell, and tab membership or layout change.

tests/herdr.test.sh: the fake Herdr must report agent_status the way real Herdr does, keeping 'working' after the agent process has exited. Name that observed behaviour in the fixture, not a value chosen to make the code pass. Fail-first cases: a completed run whose pane is an idle shell with agent_status still 'working' is closed; the same run with a busy shell is retained; a blocked result is retained; an identity mismatch is retained. Evidence is the pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates; this task does not require the worker to execute tests itself.

tasks.title: captain's board layout parity with the 2026-09-20 prototype
acceptance: Captain decision D-047 chose option B: full layout parity with design/proposals/2026-09-20-captain-board/prototype.html, without invented percentages. This task's own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.
